title: Existing-position exit rules — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #28 (portfolio-exit-rules), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: evaluate_exit_flags() recomputes several indicators from scratch on overlapping windows within a single call: protective_stop(position, daily_ohlcv[:-1]) computes EMA(13) over the pre-today slice, autoenvelope(daily_ohlcv['close']) separately computes EMA(13) over the full (today-inclusive) series, and evaluate_impulse(daily_ohlcv) recomputes EMA(13) + the MACD-Histogram yet again over that same full series -- three independent EMA(13) passes plus a MACD pass per call. evaluate_tide() is also called twice (full weekly_ohlcv, then weekly_ohlcv[:-1]), each independently recomputing MACD-Histogram + EMA(13)/EMA(26) over its own slice. None of this is a correctness issue (mirrors the already-tracked, analogous finding in signal-engine-orchestration-followups for engine.py/impulse.py) and isn't a hot path yet at current per-position, on-demand evaluation call volumes, but worth revisiting -- e.g. sharing the EMA/MACD series across protective_stop/autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse, or a slice-aware cache -- next time exits.py, risk.py, autoenvelope.py, or impulse.py is touched, especially once this feeds a portfolio-wide endpoint evaluating every held position on each request.

The 'six_percent_rule_contributor' decision recorded in docs/tasks/portfolio-exit-rules.json claims 'stop_hit and six_percent_rule_contributor are mutually exclusive by construction' -- but this only holds if position.current_price and daily_ohlcv's latest close represent the same 'today'. evaluate_exit_flags() takes both as independent parameters with no validation or documented precondition tying them together: stop_hit is tested against daily_ohlcv['close'].iloc[-1], while position_risk_pct (feeding both two_percent_rule_breached and six_percent_rule_contributor) is computed against position.current_price via risk.py's pre-existing contract (from the portfolio-risk-rules task, not introduced here). If a future caller (the still-stubbed GET /api/portfolio/risk endpoint, per api-portfolio-risk) ever populates these from data that isn't perfectly in sync (e.g. a stale current_price from a failed/cached price fetch while daily_ohlcv reflects a fresher bar), stop_hit and six_percent_rule_contributor could both fire together despite the decision's claim. Not a live bug today (no wired caller exists yet to violate this), and not a docs/Analyse.md violation (§7 doesn't require these flags be mutually exclusive -- that was only the task-worker's own rationale for the design, not a spec requirement), but worth either (a) adding an explicit documented precondition to evaluate_exit_flags() that daily_ohlcv's latest bar and position.current_price must be as-of the same day, or (b) softening/removing the 'by construction' claim in the decisions entry so a future reader doesn't rely on a guarantee the code doesn't actually enforce. Surface this when api-portfolio-risk (the real caller) is implemented.

decisions.decision: Fixed the redundant-computation finding by adding optional, backward-compatible precomputed-series keyword parameters to the four collaborator functions evaluate_exit_flags() calls -- protective_stop(..., short_ema=), autoenvelope(..., mid=), evaluate_impulse(..., ema_13=), and evaluate_tide(..., histogram=, ema_13=, ema_26=) -- all defaulting to None (unchanged behavior: each function still computes its own series internally when the caller doesn't supply one). evaluate_exit_flags() now computes the daily EMA(13) once (over the full, today-inclusive daily_ohlcv['close']) and shares it -- as-is with autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse, sliced via .iloc[:-1] for protective_stop's pre-today window -- and computes the weekly macd_components()/ema(13) once and shares them (again with a .iloc[:-1] slice for the 'previous tide' call) across both evaluate_tide() invocations. Slicing a full-series EMA/MACD computation to derive a shorter window's values is valid because EMA/MACD are causal (a value at index t depends only on data up to and including t, never later data) -- verified both by a hand-argument in each function's updated docstring and by a dedicated unmocked regression test (TestEvaluateTidePrecomputedSeries.test_precomputed_series_causal_slice_matches_recomputing_on_truncated_series in test_triple_screen.py) confirming the sliced-and-shared result exactly equals independently recomputing on the truncated series. This reduces the daily side from 3 independent EMA(13) passes to 1, and the weekly side from 2 independent macd_components()+ema(13) passes to 1 each, per evaluate_exit_flags() call -- verified via call-counting spy tests wrapping the real (unmocked) ema/macd_components functions (TestSharedIndicatorComputation in test_portfolio_exits.py), not just mocked-return assertions, so a regression back to independent recomputation would be caught.
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected: (1) reimplementing the shared math directly inside exits.py using the low-level ema()/macd_components() primitives instead of going through protective_stop/autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse/evaluate_tide at all -- rejected because it would duplicate each function's own business logic (protective_stop's swing-low-window/volatility-buffer formula, autoenvelope's rolling-deviation-band formula, evaluate_impulse's GREEN/RED/BLUE decision table, evaluate_tide's BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL table) inside exits.py, creating a second place each could silently drift from its own module's documented contract -- worse for maintainability than the redundant-computation cost it would save. (2) leaving the redundancy entirely deferred, matching the still-unresolved sibling finding in signal-engine-orchestration-followups -- rejected because this specific followups task's checklist wording ('worth revisiting ... next time exits.py, risk.py, autoenvelope.py, or impulse.py is touched') explicitly names this task's own scope as the right moment, unlike the sibling task where no dedicated follow-up task session was addressing those exact files. (3) a slice-aware LRU-style cache keyed by (id(dataframe), window) instead of explicit parameter-passing -- rejected as needing identity-based cache keys on mutable, unhashable pandas objects (fragile, easy to get wrong across process/test boundaries) for no benefit over the simpler explicit-parameter approach, since evaluate_exit_flags() already has direct, single-call-site control over both the daily and weekly series. Optional keyword-only parameters (not positional, not required) were chosen specifically so every existing caller of protective_stop/autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse/evaluate_tide elsewhere in the codebase (engine.py, their own existing test suites) continues to work completely unchanged -- confirmed by the full 330-test suite passing with no test modifications required in those other call sites.

decisions.decision: Resolved the same-day precondition finding via option (a) from the checklist item -- added an explicit 'Precondition' section to evaluate_exit_flags()'s docstring in exits.py stating that daily_ohlcv's latest bar and position.current_price must represent the same trading day, that the function does not validate this, and that 'stop_hit'/'six_percent_rule_contributor' mutual exclusivity only holds when that precondition is met -- rather than adding a runtime check that raises when it's violated.
decisions.rationale: A runtime check was considered and rejected as infeasible with the current data contract, not merely undesirable: neither Position (app/portfolio/models.py -- current_price: float | None, with no associated as-of timestamp/date field) nor the daily_ohlcv DataFrame contract this function and protective_stop/autoenvelope/evaluate_impulse already share (lowercase OHLCV columns only, no date column required or guaranteed -- confirmed against every existing caller/test fixture in the test suite, none of which include a date column) carries a date this function could compare. Adding one would mean extending Position's schema (which is also the pydantic model layer the not-yet-implemented GET/POST /api/portfolio endpoints and their OpenAPI contract will be built on) and/or requiring every daily_ohlcv caller to start carrying a date column it doesn't today -- a materially larger, cross-cutting schema change well beyond this followups task's scope, and one that the still-stubbed api-portfolio-risk task (the only prospective real caller) is better positioned to decide when it actually wires a caller and knows what date information it has available (e.g. from the OHLCV cache's own `date` column in app/db/models.py, which does exist at the DB layer but isn't threaded through to this function's DataFrame contract). Documenting the precondition now, rather than silently leaving the earlier 'mutually exclusive by construction' claim unqualified, means a future reader (including api-portfolio-risk's implementer) is warned rather than misled; option (b) (softening/removing the claim entirely) was not chosen in addition, since the claim is accurate and worth keeping as a statement of the *intended* contract -- it's the missing precondition documentation, not the claim itself, that was the gap. This clarifies, without retracting, the 'mutually exclusive by construction' claim recorded in docs/tasks/portfolio-exit-rules.json's decisions array (the six_percent_rule_contributor decision) by making its same-day precondition explicit in code.

decisions.decision: Fixed pr-reviewer's blocking finding on PR #29 (evaluate_exit_flags() raising a bare KeyError('close') instead of the documented ValueError for a daily_ohlcv missing 'close') by extracting protective_stop()'s existing column/empty validation out of risk.py's protective_stop() into a new module-level function risk.validate_daily_ohlcv_columns(daily_ohlcv), then calling that validator as the very first statement in evaluate_exit_flags() -- before daily_close = daily_ohlcv['close'] or any other column access -- while leaving the rest of the function (including the daily/weekly EMA/MACD-sharing this task's earlier decisions entry added) unchanged. protective_stop() itself now just calls the extracted validator instead of inlining the checks, so its own behavior/error messages/tests are unaffected. Added a regression test (test_real_malformed_daily_ohlcv_missing_close_raises_value_error_not_key_error in TestEvaluateExitFlagsEndToEnd, test_portfolio_exits.py) asserting evaluate_exit_flags() raises ValueError (matching 'missing required column') rather than KeyError for a daily_ohlcv missing 'close' -- reproduced the bug against the pre-fix code first (confirmed it raised KeyError('close') as the review predicted) before applying the fix, to be sure the test actually exercises the regression.
decisions.rationale: Considered and rejected: (1) simply reordering the existing code so protective_stop() is called before daily_close/daily_ema_13 are computed, letting protective_stop's own inline validation run first as it did pre-PR -- rejected because protective_stop() needs an already-computed short_ema to share (this task's earlier decisions entry's whole point), creating a circular ordering requirement: sharing needs daily_ema_13 computed before protective_stop is called, but validation-first needs protective_stop's check to run before daily_ohlcv['close'] is touched at all. Preserving both properties simultaneously requires the validation logic to be available independently of computing the EMA, which is exactly what extracting it into a standalone function accomplishes. (2) duplicating the two validation lines (empty check + missing-column check) directly at the top of evaluate_exit_flags() instead of extracting a shared function -- rejected because it creates two independent copies of the same contract that could silently drift (e.g. a future change to protective_stop's required-column set or error message would need to be manually mirrored in exits.py, with nothing enforcing that); a single shared function callable from both call sites removes that drift risk entirely, at the cost of one small, well-documented cross-module function. (3) leaving evaluate_exit_flags() to validate only 'close' (the column it accesses directly) rather than protective_stop's full {'low', 'close'} set -- rejected because evaluate_exit_flags() also always calls protective_stop() further down in the same call (irrespective of which flags end up firing), so a daily_ohlcv missing 'low' would still hit protective_stop's own validation moments later regardless; validating the same full set up front just makes that failure happen at the top of the function instead of a few lines in, with an identical resulting exception either way, and keeps the single validator's contract simple ('the columns protective_stop requires') rather than two different partial-validation entry points needing to be kept in sync.

comments.summary: First review pass (2026-09-15T19:48:00Z) found one blocking issue: evaluate_exit_flags() raised a bare KeyError instead of the documented ValueError for a malformed daily_ohlcv missing 'close', because daily_close = daily_ohlcv['close'] ran before protective_stop's own column validation. This was fixed correctly and completely in commit 3089cb7 -- verified: validate_daily_ohlcv_columns(daily_ohlcv) is genuinely the first statement in evaluate_exit_flags(), running before any daily_ohlcv column access; protective_stop() now calls the same extracted function with byte-for-byte identical checks/error messages (confirmed via its untouched, still-passing pre-existing tests); the fewer-than-2-rows path still raises correctly via protective_stop's own call on the empty .iloc[:-1] slice; and the new regression test (test_real_malformed_daily_ohlcv_missing_close_raises_value_error_not_key_error) genuinely reproduces and catches the original bug (commit message records it was confirmed to fail pre-fix).

Blocking (new, found via code-review skill dispatched during this re-review): evaluate_exit_flags() has the identical KeyError-instead-of-ValueError gap on the weekly side that the daily-side fix (3089cb7) was supposed to close. `weekly_close = weekly_ohlcv["close"]` (around line 154) runs with no column validation of weekly_ohlcv anywhere in the function. Reproduced directly against HEAD (3089cb7): evaluate_exit_flags(position, account, daily_ohlcv, weekly_ohlcv_missing_close, portfolio_open_risk_pct=0.0) raises KeyError('close'), not ValueError. No test in test_portfolio_exits.py covers a malformed weekly_ohlcv. Scope note: this specific failure mode is not a new regression introduced by this PR -- checked evaluate_tide()'s body against the PR #28 baseline (commit bf64584) and it already did weekly_close = weekly_ohlcv['close'] with no column validation of its own, so this bug predates this PR. What makes it blocking now: (a) evaluate_exit_flags() also has its own new direct, unguarded weekly_ohlcv['close'] access at the top level (added by this task's own weekly MACD/EMA-sharing change), and (b) this PR's own fix commit set out specifically to make evaluate_exit_flags()'s malformed-OHLCV handling raise the documented ValueError, and the fixed function's docstring now claims 'ValueError: for a malformed daily_ohlcv (empty, or missing a required column) -- validated up front' with no equivalent claim or guard for weekly_ohlcv, which carries the identical risk -- an incomplete, asymmetric fix to the exact contract this PR is about. Suggested fix: a validate_weekly_ohlcv_columns() (or generalized validator) called before weekly_close = weekly_ohlcv['close'], mirroring the daily-side pattern just applied.

Non-blocking (also found via the code-review skill): protective_stop() re-validates daily_ohlcv's columns a second time even though evaluate_exit_flags() already validated the identical column set moments earlier via validate_daily_ohlcv_columns() -- a small, avoidable duplication of a cheap check, not a bug. Filed as a checklist item on docs/tasks/portfolio-exit-rules-followups-followups.json rather than blocking this PR.

Everything else re-verified and unaffected by the above: full suite re-run on commit 3089cb7 -- 331/331 passing (330 + 1 new regression test), no regressions; pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing -> 99.36% repo-wide (gate 90%), exits.py/risk.py both 100% line/branch. No ruff/mypy config exists in backend/pyproject.toml, so no lint step was invented. verify-elder-signal re-run against docs/Analyse.md #7: no methodology drift, protective_stop's core formula (swing low minus volatility buffer) byte-for-byte unchanged. No API route/schema touched -- no OpenAPI snapshot check applies. No new module/dependency/layer -- architecture-review not triggered. No UI surface -- browser walkthrough explicitly not applicable, not silently skipped. The prior review's one remaining non-blocking finding (weekly MACD-Histogram computed unconditionally on <2-row weekly_ohlcv) remains correctly out of scope for this pass and stays tracked on docs/tasks/portfolio-exit-rules-followups-followups.json.

review.notes: Re-review of commit 3089cb7, the fix for the sole blocking finding from the 2026-09-15T19:48:00Z pass. gh pr checkout 29 (already checked out, working tree clean at start). First verified the daily-side fix itself is correct and complete (see comments above), re-ran the full suite (331/331 passing) and coverage (99.36%, gate 90%) myself, and ran verify-elder-signal against docs/Analyse.md #7 (no drift). Initially posted an accept based on that manual pass, per the same standard the prior needs_work-catching pass used, while a code-review skill (high effort) dispatch against the fix commit was still running in the background. That backgrounded pass then returned and surfaced a real, independently-reproduced bug (the weekly-side KeyError twin of the just-fixed daily-side one) that the manual pass had missed -- reversed the verdict to needs_work in a follow-up PR comment/review before finalizing this task JSON, rather than let the premature accept stand. Lesson for next time: wait for the backgrounded code-review result before posting a verdict rather than posting on the manual pass alone. Non-blocking duplicate-validation finding filed on docs/tasks/portfolio-exit-rules-followups-followups.json. Verdict: needs_work due to the weekly-side blocking finding. Posted as two COMMENTED-type gh pr reviews (the initial accept, then a corrective needs_work reversal) plus a plain PR comment with full findings on PR #29 -- never approve/request-changes.
